ASAD-NOTES:25:intro/r4.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:25:intro/r4.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:25:intro/r4.claim: Revelation belongs to the same majestic creative order as nature; the Prophet's complaint that followers discarded the Qur'an is especially relevant today.
ASAD-NOTES:25:intro/r4.anchor: the same majestic order of God's creative activity

STUDYQURAN:25:intro/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:25:intro/r3.speaker: A minority
STUDYQURAN:25:intro/r3.claim: A minority classifies most of the surah as Madinan but verses 68–70 as Makkan.
STUDYQURAN:25:intro/r3.anchor: while a minority consider most of the sūrah to be from the Madinan period and vv. 68–70 to be from the Makkan period

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p358/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p358/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p358/r2.claim: After recalling God’s beneficence in revelation, the verse turns to His power and oneness.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p358/r2.anchor: In the earlier verse, God has referred to His beneficence

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p359/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p359/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p359/r1.claim: Because God is sovereign, the Qur’an is the universe’s kingly directive and rejection invites a revenge no one can prevent.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p359/r1.anchor: It is the directive of the real king of this universe that has to be obeyed come what may

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p359/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p359/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p359/r2.claim: God has neither children nor partners and needs no helper to own His kingdom.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p359/r2.anchor: Neither does He have a son nor a daughter nor any partner in His sovereignty

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p359/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p359/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p359/r3.claim: Creation’s appointed measures prove oneness: lifespans, clouds, winds, sun, and moon all remain within limits set by their wise creator.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p359/r3.anchor: By their very existence, they bear witness that they have been created by a powerful and wise God

DURR-FULL:v5p581/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p581/r6.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p581/r6.claim: God formed every animal and taught it what benefits it, making human and animal forms distinct; Mujahid links this to God's creation and measurement of all things.
DURR-FULL:v5p581/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد - رضي الله عنه - في قوله: {أعطى كل شيء خلقه ثم هدى} قال: سوى خلق كل دابة ثم هداها لما يصلحها

SAMIN-DURR:25:2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:25:2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:25:2/r1.claim: The relative alladhī may be nominative as an adjective of the preceding alladhī.
SAMIN-DURR:25:2/r1.anchor: يجوز في " الذي " الرفع نعتا للذي الأول

SAMIN-DURR:25:2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:25:2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:25:2/r2.claim: Alternatively, the relative may be nominative as an explanatory apposition to the preceding alladhī.
SAMIN-DURR:25:2/r2.anchor: أو بيانا، أو بدلا، أو خبرا

SAMIN-DURR:25:2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:25:2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:25:2/r3.claim: Alternatively, it may be the predicate of an omitted subject.
SAMIN-DURR:25:2/r3.anchor: أو بدلا، أو خبرا لمبتدأ محذوف

SAMIN-DURR:25:2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:25:2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:25:2/r4.claim: A final option is accusative case as a laudatory construction.
SAMIN-DURR:25:2/r4.anchor: أو النصب على المدح. وما بعد

SAMIN-DURR:25:2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:25:2/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:25:2/r5.claim: The material after nazala still belongs to the first relative clause, so it is not an intervening foreign clause and does not disrupt attachment of the second relative as its dependent.
SAMIN-DURR:25:2/r5.anchor: وما بعد " نزل " من تمام الصلة فليس أجنبيا

SAMIN-DURR:25:2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:25:2/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:25:2/r6.claim: Here khalq means bringing into being and preparing each thing for its proper function, allowing fa-qaddarahu to add that He determined it precisely; taking khalq as determination would make the wording redundant.
SAMIN-DURR:25:2/r6.anchor: الخلق هنا عبارة عن الإحداث والتهيئة لما يصلح له

ZAJJAJ:v4p57/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p57/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p57/r4.claim: God created living creatures, determined what sustains and establishes them, and measured all this for creation with wisdom.
ZAJJAJ:v4p57/r4.anchor: خلق الله الحيوان وقدر له ما يصلحه ويقيمه، وقدر جميع ذلك لخلقه بحكمة وتقدير

ASAD-NOTES:25:1#n2/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:25:1#n2/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:25:1#n2/r1.claim: Asad refers the reader to his note 133 on 17:111.

ASAD-NOTES:25:1#n3/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:25:1#n3/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:25:1#n3/r1.claim: God assigns each individual thing or phenomenon its function, an idea also formulated in 87:2-3.
ASAD-NOTES:25:1#n3/r1.anchor: the function assigned by Him to each individual thing or phenomenon: cf. the oldest formulation of this idea in 87:2-3.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p355/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p355/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p355/r1.claim: The Qur’an’s chapter structure pairs sūrahs; al-Aḥzāb summarizes and supplements its chapter, like al-Nūr does for the preceding chapter.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p355/r1.anchor: The principle of sūrahs occurring in pairs can be witnessed in this chapter also

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p355/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p355/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p355/r2.claim: Across the chapter are the phases of Muhammad’s mission—warning, migration, and war—and the core themes of monotheism, prophethood, and the Hereafter; its reasoning style is distinct.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p355/r2.anchor: All phases of the preaching mission of Prophet Muḥammad (sws) – warning, migration and war – as well as all basic topics as monotheism, prophethood and the hereafter are also discussed.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p355/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p355/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p355/r3.claim: The chapter’s comprehensive theme is affirming prophethood: it answers Quraysh and allies on Muhammad’s prophethood and the Qur’an’s divinity, explains their true status, promises believers reward after trial, and warns persistent deniers after conclusive proof.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p355/r3.anchor: The comprehensive theme of this sūrah is affirmation of prophethood.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p355/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p355/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p355/r4.claim: Al-Furqān defends the Qur’an and Prophet by answering opponents’ objections, alluding to their motives, and arguing further on issues they resist, including monotheism and punishment.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p355/r4.anchor: The theme of this sūrah is to defend the Qur’ ān and the Prophet (sws).

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p355/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p355/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p355/r5.claim: In verses 1–9, the Qur’an is a blessed, merciful revelation, yet deniers of monotheism and the Hereafter call it a fabrication and conspiracy.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p355/r5.anchor: The Qur’ ān has been revealed by the most blessed being as the most blessed and merciful thing.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p355/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p355/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p355/r6.claim: The opening passage points to opponents’ propaganda intended to turn people away from the Prophet and the Qur’an.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p355/r6.anchor: A reference is made to the propaganda worked by the opponents of the Prophet (sws) to lead people away from him and the Qur’ān.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p79/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p79/r18.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p79/r18.claim: The previous sura said that everything in heaven and earth belongs to God; this verse adds that He rules and subdues heaven, earth, and their contents, joining ownership and dominion.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p79/r18.anchor: ولما سبق في أواخر السورة ألا إن لله ما في السموات والأرض

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p79/r19.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p79/r19.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p79/r19.claim: The relative al-ladhī can be set off for praise in nominative or accusative, or construed as an adjective or appositive of the first al-ladhī; the following clause remains part of its relative clause.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p79/r19.anchor: والذي مقطوع للمدح رفعا أو نصبا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p80/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p80/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p80/r1.claim: God did not adopt anyone as a child; this rebuts Quraysh, Christians, and Jews who ascribe offspring to Him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p80/r1.anchor: الظاهر نفي الاتخاذ أي لم ينزل أحدا منزلة الولد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p80/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p80/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p80/r2.claim: An alternative says God has no child, as in “He did not beget,” since procreation is impossible for Him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p80/r2.anchor: لم يكن له ولد بمعنى قوله لم يلد لأن التوالد مستحيل عليه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p80/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p80/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p80/r3.claim: The denial of a partner reinforces God's ownership of heaven and earth and rejects those who assign Him one.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p80/r3.anchor: تأكيد لقوله له ملك السماوات والأرض ورد على من جعل لله شريكا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p80/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p80/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p80/r4.claim: “Everything” is general, encompassing created entities and their actions.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p80/r4.anchor: وخلق كل شيء عام في خلق الذوات وأفعالها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p80/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p80/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p80/r5.claim: One proposed an omitted qualification, “everything whose creation is valid,” to exclude God's essence and eternal attributes.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p80/r5.anchor: وفي الكلام حذف تقديره وخلق كل شيء مما يصح خلقه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p80/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p80/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p80/r6.claim: No qualification is needed: “I honored every man” does not include the speaker, just as this universal excludes God and His eternal attributes.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p80/r6.anchor: ولا يحتاج إلى هذا المحذوف لأن من قال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p80/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p80/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p80/r7.claim: If creation means measuring, “then He measured it” risks repeating the same meaning.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p80/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p80/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p80/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says God brought each thing into existence in due proportion and prepared it for what suits it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p80/r8.anchor: فقال الزمخشري: المعنى أنه أحدث كل شيء إحداثا مراعى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p80/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p80/r9.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p80/r9.claim: Alternatively, God's wise creation brings each thing into existence according to a measure, without disparity.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p80/r9.anchor: إلا على وجه التقدير من غير تفاوت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p80/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p80/r10.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p80/r10.claim: Another explanation treats “created” as simply produced, then measured in its coming to be.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p80/r10.anchor: وأوجد كل شيء فقدره في إيجاده متفاوتا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p80/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p80/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p80/r11.claim: Another view says God assigned each thing an endpoint, measuring its persistence to a known term.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p80/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p80/r12.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p80/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya defines measuring things by place, time, quantity, benefit, and precision.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p80/r12.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: تقدير الأشياء هو حدها بالأمكنة والأزمان

ALUSI-FULL:v18p232#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p232#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p232#2/r1.claim: God alone possesses the sovereign dominion of heaven and earth and all within them, entailing complete power and disposal over creation, destruction, life, death, commands, and prohibitions according to wise will.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p232#2/r1.anchor: أي له سبحانه خاصة دون غيره لا استقلالا ولا اشتراكا السلطان القاهر والاستيلاء الباهر عليهما المستلزم للقدرة التامة والتصرف الكلي

ALUSI-FULL:v18p232#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p232#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p232#2/r2.claim: The relative may be nominative as the predicate of an omitted subject, an adjective, explanatory apposition, or a substitute for the earlier relative; it may also be nominative or accusative as praise.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p232#2/r2.anchor: ومحل الموصول الرفع على أنه خبر لمبتدأ محذوف والجملة مستانفة مقررة لما قبلها أو على أنه نعت للموصول أو بيان له أو بدل منه

ALUSI-FULL:v18p232#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p232#2/r3.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v18p232#2/r3.claim: Al-Tibi prefers a nominative substitute because the relative clause was not known to the adversaries and thus explains the earlier relative; al-Alusi calls this far-fetched.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p232#2/r3.anchor: واختار الطيبي أن محله الرفع على الإبدال وعلله بقوله لأن من حق الصلة أن تكون معلومة عند المخاطب

ALUSI-FULL:v18p232#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p232#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p232#2/r4.claim: God has not assigned anyone the status of a child; alternatively, He has no child, contrary to claims about Christ, Ezra, or angels.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p232#2/r4.anchor: أي لم ينزل أحدا منزلة الولد وقيل أي لم يكن ولد كما يزعم الذين يقولون في حق المسيح وعزير والملائكة

ALUSI-FULL:v18p232#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p232#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p232#2/r5.claim: The denial of a partner expressly refutes dualists who posit multiple gods, although God’s exclusive ownership already entails that there is no partner.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p232#2/r5.anchor: وأفرد بالذكر مع أن ما ذكر من اختصاص ملكهما به تعالى مستلزم له قطعا للتصريح ببطلان زعم الثنوية القائلين بتعدد الآلهة

ALUSI-FULL:v18p232#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p232#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p232#2/r6.claim: The denial of a child is placed between exclusive ownership and denial of a partner to assert its independent force and prevent it from seeming a continuation of the first clause.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p232#2/r6.anchor: وتوسيط نفي اتخاذ الولد بينهما للتنبيه على استقلاله وأصالته والاحتراز عن توهم كونه تتمة للأول

ALUSI-FULL:v18p232#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p232#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p232#2/r7.claim: God brought everything into existence in measured, proportionate form according to His wise will, as with the human being’s particular materials, forms, and shapes.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p232#2/r7.anchor: أي أحدثه إحداثا جاريا على سنن التقدير والتسوية حسبما اقتضته إرادته المبنية على الحكم البالغة

ALUSI-FULL:v18p232#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p232#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p232#2/r8.claim: God equipped each created thing with the properties and actions suited to its purpose; for humans these include understanding, reflection, livelihood, crafts, and varied work.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p232#2/r8.anchor: فقدره ( أي هيأه لما أراد به من الخصائص والأفعال اللائقة به

ALUSI-FULL:v18p233/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p233/r1.speaker: الزجاج
ALUSI-FULL:v18p233/r1.claim: Al-Zajjaj’s preferred reading distinguishes creation as proportioning from تقدير as preparing for purpose, so the wording is not repetitive; alternatively creation means bringing into existence and explicit تقدير separately marks the measured manner of each creation.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p233/r1.anchor: فلا تكرار في الآية لما ظهر من أن التقدير الدال عليه الخلق بمعنى التسوية والمعبر عنه بلفظه بمعنى التهيئة

ALUSI-FULL:v18p233/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p233/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p233/r2.claim: Another view takes the second تقدير as assigning each thing its lifespan and sustaining it until its appointed term.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p233/r2.anchor: وقيل التقدير الثاني هو التقدير للبقاء إلى الأجل المسمى فكأنه قيل وأوجد كل شيء على سنن التقدير فأدامه

ALUSI-FULL:v18p233/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p233/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p233/r3.claim: The proposed inversion in the wording does not remove the apparent repetition unless one of the preceding explanations is adopted.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p233/r3.anchor: وزعم بعضهم أن في الكلام قلبا وهو على ما فيه لا يدفع لزوم التكرار بدون أحد الأوجه المذكورة

ALUSI-FULL:v18p233/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p233/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p233/r4.claim: Universal creation refutes dualists who assign evil and good to different creators, and is also directed against the Muʿtazilite account of voluntary creaturely acts.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p233/r4.anchor: وفيها رد على الثنوية القائلين بأن خالق الشر غير خالف الخير ولا يضر كونه معلوما مما تقدم

ALUSI-FULL:v18p233/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p233/r5.speaker: إرشاد العقل السليم
ALUSI-FULL:v18p233/r5.claim: The clause explains the preceding denials: since God created all things, everything else lies under His dominion, so none can be His child or partner.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p233/r5.anchor: أنها جارية مجرى العليل لما قبلها من الجمل المنتظمة في سلك الصلة

ALUSI-FULL:v18p233/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p233/r6.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v18p233/r6.claim: Al-Tibi views exclusive ownership as a prelude to denying child and partner, then creation as a further reason that God’s status as originator and owner precludes both; the text links this to the denial of a child in 6:101.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p233/r6.anchor: وذكر الطيبي أن قوله تعالى : ( له ملك السماوات والأرض )

ALUSI-FULL:v18p233/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p233/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p233/r7.claim: Al-Alusi adds that creation may state explicitly what was already implicit, intensifying the condemnation of the polytheists in the following cited verse.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p233/r7.anchor: وقد يقال : إن هذه الجملة تصريح بما علم قبل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p69#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p69#2/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p69#2/r8.claim: God created everything that can be described by the attribute of being created.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p69#2/r8.anchor: وخلق كل شيء} مما يطلق عليه صفة المخلوق

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p69#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p69#2/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p69#2/r9.claim: God perfected each thing and prepared it for what suits it, without flaw or disparity.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p69#2/r9.anchor: {فقدره تقديرا} فسواه وهيأه لما يصلح له، لا خلل فيه ولا تفاوت

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p69#2/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p69#2/r10.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p69#2/r10.claim: Another view says God assigned every thing its measure, including lifespan and provision, and the decrees unfolded according to His creation.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p69#2/r10.anchor: وقيل: قدر لكل شيء تقديرا من الأجل والرزق، فجرت المقادير على ما خلق

BAYDAWI-FULL:25:2/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:2/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:2/r1.claim: The clause describing dominion may be an appositive to the first noun, or an expression of praise in the nominative or accusative.
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:2/r1.anchor: بدل من الأول أو مدح مرفوع أو منصوب

BAYDAWI-FULL:25:2/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:2/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:2/r2.claim: The denial of a child refutes the Christian claim.

BAYDAWI-FULL:25:2/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:2/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:2/r3.claim: The denial of a partner refutes the dualists; God has absolute dominion without a rival or co-owner.
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:2/r3.anchor: كقول الثنوية أثبت له الملك مطلقا ونفى ما يقوم مقامه

BAYDAWI-FULL:25:2/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:2/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:2/r4.claim: He originated everything with measures suited to His will, including human materials, forms, and shapes.
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:2/r4.anchor: أحدثه إحداثا مراعى فيه التقدير حسب إرادته

BAYDAWI-FULL:25:2/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:2/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:2/r5.claim: He prepared each creature for its intended traits and acts, fitting humans for perception, understanding, judgment, invention, and work.
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:2/r5.anchor: فقدره وهيأه لما أراد منه من الخصائص والأفعال

BAYDAWI-FULL:25:2/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:2/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:2/r6.claim: Alternatively, He appointed each creature's duration until its specified term.
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:2/r6.anchor: أو { فقدره } للبقاء إلى أجل مسمى

BAYDAWI-FULL:25:2/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:2/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:2/r7.claim: If khalq means mere bringing into existence, He created each thing and measured its production so it would not be uneven.
BAYDAWI-FULL:25:2/r7.anchor: وأوجد كل شيء فقدره في إيجاده حتى لا يكون متفاوتا

BIQAI-FULL:v5p294/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p294/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p294/r1.claim: After mentioning the revealer, the Furqān, and its recipient generally, the passage now details them in that order, beginning with God as sole sovereign and the universal scope of His message.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p294/r1.anchor: ذكر الفرقان والمنزل عليه على طريق الإجمال , أتبع ذلك تفصيله

BIQAI-FULL:v5p294/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p294/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p294/r2.claim: Because God alone owns the heavens and earth, there is no reason to deny that He sends a messenger to everyone within them.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p294/r2.anchor: فلا إنكار لأن يرسل رسولا إلى كل من فيهما

BIQAI-FULL:v5p294/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p294/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p294/r3.claim: God has no child who could act arrogantly toward His messenger.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p294/r3.anchor: ولم يتخذ ولدا } ليتكبر على رسوله

BIQAI-FULL:v5p294/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p294/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p294/r4.claim: No partner can oppose or share God's messengership, leaving some creation outside His message or subject to another's command.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p294/r4.anchor: في الملك } ليناقضه في الرسالة أو يقاسمه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p294/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p294/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p294/r5.claim: A thing's inability to cross its created limit or change its kind demonstrates that it is created and governed; creatures cannot fully explain this constraint.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p294/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p294/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p294/r6.claim: Khalaqa means bringing something into existence with due measure and proportion.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p294/r6.anchor: أحدث إحداثا مراعي فيه التقدير والتسوية

BIQAI-FULL:v5p294/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p294/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p294/r7.claim: Everything includes alleged divine offspring, partners, and all else; God fitted each thing without disparity for its proper purpose and enabled it for that end.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p294/r7.anchor: أي مما ادعى فيه الولدية أو الشرك وغيره

DURR-FULL:v6p234/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p234/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v6p234/r1.claim: The surah is Meccan and consists of seventy-seven verses.
DURR-FULL:v6p234/r1.anchor: مكية وآياتها سبع وسبعون مقدمة سورة الفرقان

DURR-FULL:v6p234/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p234/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p234/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Surat al-Furqan was revealed in Mecca.
DURR-FULL:v6p234/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: نزلت سورة الفرقان بمكة

DURR-FULL:v6p234/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p234/r3.speaker: ابن الزبير
DURR-FULL:v6p234/r3.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr also reports that Surat al-Furqan was revealed in Mecca.
DURR-FULL:v6p234/r3.anchor: عن ابن الزبير قال: نزلت بمكة سورة الفرقان

DURR-FULL:v6p234/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p234/r4.speaker: النبي ﷺ
DURR-FULL:v6p234/r4.claim: Umar challenged Hisham ibn Hakim's unfamiliar recitation of Surat al-Furqan; the Prophet approved both men's readings as revealed and said the Qur'an came down in seven modes, so recite what is easy.
DURR-FULL:v6p234/r4.anchor: عن عمر بن الخطاب قال: سمعت هشام بن حكيم يقرأ سورة الفرقان في حياة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR-FULL:v6p234/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p234/r5.speaker: النبي ﷺ
DURR-FULL:v6p234/r5.claim: Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman reports that after the Prophet omitted a verse of Surat al-Furqan in dawn prayer, Ubay ibn Kaʿb said he had mistaken it for an abrogated verse; the Prophet corrected him.
DURR-FULL:v6p234/r5.anchor: عن حميد بن عبد الرحمن بن عوف أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم صلى الصبح فقرأ سورة الفرقان فاسقط آية

DURR-FULL:v6p235/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p235/r4.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p235/r4.claim: Qatāda explains that God determined what is beneficial for every created thing and assigned it a known measure.
DURR-FULL:v6p235/r4.anchor: قال: بين لكل شيء من خلقه صلاحه وجعل ذلك بقدر معلوم

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2661/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2661/r1.speaker: جبريل
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2661/r1.claim: Gabriel tells Muhammad that God owns all creation—the heavens, earths, their inhabitants, and what is known or unknown—and that nothing resembles the Lord in the attributes made known to Muhammad.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2661/r1.anchor: عن الضحاك ، عن عبد الله بن عباس قال : قال جبريل : يا محمد لله الخلق كله السماوات كلهن ومن فيهن

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2661/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2661/r2.speaker: عكرمة
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2661/r2.claim: ʿIkrima reports Jews calling ʿUzayr God’s son, Christians calling the Messiah God’s son, Sabeans worshipping angels, Magians worshipping the sun and moon, and idolaters worshipping idols; the denial refutes these claims.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2661/r2.anchor: عن عكرمة قال : قالت اليهود عزير ابن الله وقالت النصارى المسيح ابن الله

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2661/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2661/r3.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2661/r3.claim: Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb al-Quraẓī says Jews and Christians claimed God had a child, Arabs included a partner in the talbiya except one belonging to God, and Sabeans and Magians posited divine allies; the verse denies child and partner.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2661/r3.anchor: عن القرظي محمد بن كعب في هذه الاية : ولم يكن له شريك في الملك

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2661/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2661/r4.speaker: عزير
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2661/r4.claim: Wahb ibn Munabbih transmits ʿUzayr’s prayer praising God for forming bodies in wombs, giving them limbs, senses, life, nourishment and sustenance, teaching them scripture, decreeing death, and restoring them.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2661/r4.anchor: حدثني عبد الصمد بن معقل انه سمع عمه وهب بن منبه يقول : قال عزير اللهم رب انك تسميت الرحمن الرحيم

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2662/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2662/r1.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2662/r1.claim: Qatāda says God created each thing according to its nature and soundness and assigned it a known measure.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2662/r1.anchor: عن قتادة قوله : وخلق كل شيء فقدره تقديرا من خلقه وصلاحه وجعل ذلك بقدر معلوم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p317#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p317#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p317#2/r1.claim: Four attributes of God follow the relative pronoun: two that the audience already accepts frame two disputed claims, which thereby also acquire a familiar footing.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p317#2/r1.anchor: أجريت على اسم الله تعالى هذه الصفات الأربع بطريق تعريف الموصولية لأن بعض الصلات معروف عند المخاطبين اتصاف الله به

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p317#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p317#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p317#2/r2.claim: The polytheists accepted God as owner of heaven and earth and creator of everything but nevertheless attributed a child and a partner in dominion to Him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p317#2/r2.anchor: فإن المشركين ما كانوا يمترون في أن الله هو مالك السماوات والأرض ولا في أن الله هو خالق كل شيء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p317#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p317#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p317#2/r3.claim: The undisputed ownership and creation claims bracket the contested claims as premise and conclusion: an owner of such a vast realm needs neither child nor partner, and wise action is never futile.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p317#2/r3.anchor: ومن بديع النظم أن جعل الوصفان المختلف فيهما معهم متوسطين بين الوصفين اللذين لا مرية فيهما حتى يكون الوصفان المسلمين كالدليل أولا والنتيجة آخرا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p317#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p317#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p317#2/r4.claim: The second “who” clause is apposition to “the one who sent down the Criterion” in 25:1; repeating it marks the shift from gratitude for revelation to God's oneness, and dominion entails exclusive sovereignty.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p317#2/r4.anchor: فقوله : الذي له ملك السموات والأرض } بدل من { الذي نزل الفرقان }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p317#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p317#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p317#2/r5.claim: Creation means bringing every existent into being, from the greatest things to the smallest.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p317#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p317#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p317#2/r6.claim: God assigned everything a fixed measure and limit rather than creating by chance, fitting each thing precisely for its purpose without flaw; this implies deliberate will and knowledge, as in 54:49 and 13:17.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p317#2/r6.anchor: ومعنى { قدره } جعله على مقدار وحد معين لا مجرد مصادفة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p317#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p317#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p317#2/r7.claim: The cognate accusative taqdīran intensifies the point that God's act of measuring is complete in kind.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p317#2/r7.anchor: وتأكيد الفعل بالمفعول المطلق بقوله : تقديرا }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p319#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p319#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p319#2/r3.claim: The contrast between God's not taking a child and the polytheists taking other gods is a rhetorical antithesis.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p319#2/r3.anchor: وبين قوله : { ولم يتخذ ولدا } ( الفرقان : 2 ) وقوله : { واتخذوا من دونه آلهة } محسن الطباق

BURSEVI:v6p137/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p137/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p137/r1.claim: God alone, independently or jointly, owns sovereignty over the heavens and earth; mulk is authority to command and forbid among the people.
BURSEVI:v6p137/r1.anchor: له} خاصة دون غيره استقلالا أو اشتراكا

BURSEVI:v6p137/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p137/r2.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v6p137/r2.claim: Al-Kashifi glosses the phrase as God’s kingship over the heavens and earth, since He created them and is entitled to rule them.

BURSEVI:v6p137/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p137/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p137/r3.claim: In reply to Jews and Christians, God has no child to inherit His kingdom because He does not die.
BURSEVI:v6p137/r3.anchor: ردا على اليهود والنصارى : {ولم يتخذ ولدا} ليرث ملكه

BURSEVI:v6p137/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p137/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p137/r4.claim: The clause about not taking a child is coordinated with the preceding nominal clause.
BURSEVI:v6p137/r4.anchor: وهو عطف على ما قبله من الجملة الظرفية

BURSEVI:v6p137/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p137/r5.speaker: المفردات
BURSEVI:v6p137/r5.claim: Al-Mufradat derives ittakhadha from akhadha and says walad applies to singular or plural, young or old, male or female.
BURSEVI:v6p137/r5.anchor: المفردات" : تخذ بمعنى أخذ واتخذ افتعل منه والولد المولود

BURSEVI:v6p137/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p137/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p137/r6.claim: In reply to Quraysh, God has no partner in the heavens’ and earth’s sovereignty to contend with Him or assist in creating.
BURSEVI:v6p137/r6.anchor: ردا على قريش : {ولم يكن له شريك فى الملك} أي : في ملك السموات

BURSEVI:v6p137/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p137/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p137/r7.claim: A couplet from the Mathnawi underscores that God alone rules His kingdom and that only a fool would call another His partner.

BURSEVI:v6p137#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p137#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p137#2/r1.claim: God brought every existent thing into being from particular materials in specific forms, endowing it with diverse powers and properties and effects.
BURSEVI:v6p137#2/r1.anchor: أحدث كل موجود من الموجودات من مواد مخصوصة على صور معينة ورتب فيه قوى وخواص مختلفة الأحكام والآثار

BURSEVI:v6p137#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p137#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p137#2/r2.claim: He fitted each thing to its intended properties and actions: humans can understand, reflect on worldly and next-worldly affairs, devise crafts, and perform varied work, as other kinds are fitted to their functions.
BURSEVI:v6p137#2/r2.anchor: فهيأه لما أراده منه من الخصائص والأفعال اللائقة به كهيئة الإنسان للإدراك والفهم والنظر والتدبر في أمور المعاش والمعاد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p199#3/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p199#3/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p199#3/r10.claim: The verse refutes Quraysh's claims that God has a partner or daughters, including the formula in their talbiya that named a partner belonging to Him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p199#3/r10.anchor: هي من الرد على قريش في قولهم إن لله شريكا، وفي قولهم اتخذ البنات، وفي قولهم في التلبية إلا شريك هو لك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p199#3/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p199#3/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p199#3/r11.claim: “Everything” is general for all created things; God's determining fixes their places, times, measures, benefit, and perfection.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p199#3/r11.anchor: وقوله خلق كل شيء، هو عام في كل مخلوق وتقدير الأشياء هو حدها بالأمكنة والأزمان والمقادير

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p199#3/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p199#3/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p199#3/r12.claim: After describing divine attributes, the passage attacks Quraysh's gods, which lack those attributes and therefore cannot rationally be gods.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p199#3/r12.anchor: ثم عقب تعالى ذكر هذه الصفات التي هي للألوهية بالطعن على قريش في اتخاذهم آلهة ليست لهم هذه الصفات

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p72/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p72/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p72/r1.claim: One view is that God fashioned and prepared each thing for what suits it, without flaw or disparity.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p72/r1.anchor: أحدها سواه وهيأه لما يصلح له فلا خلل فيه ولا تفاوت

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p72/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p72/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p72/r2.claim: Another view is that God apportioned for each thing what would set it right and sustain it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p72/r2.anchor: والثاني قدر له ما يصلحه ويقيمه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p72/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p72/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p72/r3.claim: A third view is that God determined each thing's lifespan and provision.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p72/r3.anchor: والثالث قدر له تقديرا من الأجل والرزق

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p92#3/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p92#3/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p92#3/r4.claim: The Sender owns the heavens and earth, brings anything into being by saying Be, and alone gives life and death; Ibn Kathir connects this to 7:158.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p92#3/r4.anchor: الذي أرسلني هو مالك السموات والأرض، الذي يقول للشيء كن فيكون، وهو الذي يحيي ويميت

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p92#3/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p92#3/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p92#3/r5.claim: God declares Himself free of having a child or a partner in sovereignty.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p92#3/r5.anchor: فنزه نفسه عن الولد، وعن الشريك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p92#3/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p92#3/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p92#3/r6.claim: Everything besides God is created and owned by Him; all things fall under His mastery, subjection, governance, and decree.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p92#3/r6.anchor: كل شيء مما سواه مخلوق مربوب، وهو خالق كل شيء وربه ومليكه وإلهه

JISHUMI:v7p5264/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5264/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5264/r8.claim: Taqdīr can mean doing a thing according to a measure.

JISHUMI:v7p5264/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5264/r9.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v7p5264/r9.claim: Another gloss takes taqdīr as a thing's stability at a measure.

JISHUMI:v7p5264/r21.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5264/r21.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5264/r21.claim: God is not a body or powerful through a distinct power; He is powerful, knowing, living in Himself, able to create the heavens and earth, and so cannot take a child.
JISHUMI:v7p5264/r21.anchor: أشار إلى أنه ليس بجسم، ولا قادر بقدرة؛ بل هو قادر لذاته، عالم لذاته، حي يقدر

JISHUMI:v7p5264/r22.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5264/r22.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5264/r22.claim: God has no child to inherit His dominion.
JISHUMI:v7p5264/r22.anchor: ومن كان بهذه الصفة لا يجوز عليه اتخاذ الولد

JISHUMI:v7p5264/r23.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5264/r23.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5264/r23.claim: No partner competes with God or prevents His will.
JISHUMI:v7p5264/r23.anchor: ولم يكن له شريك في الملك يزاحمه ويمنعه من مراده

JISHUMI:v7p5264/r24.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5264/r24.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5264/r24.claim: “Everything” means everything to which the name created applies.
JISHUMI:v7p5264/r24.anchor: وخلق كل شيء مما يطلق عليه اسم المخلوق

JISHUMI:v7p5264/r25.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5264/r25.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v7p5264/r25.claim: One explanation says God measured each thing in a way that accords with wisdom.
JISHUMI:v7p5264/r25.anchor: فقدره تقديرا قيل: تقدير يوافق الحكمة،

JISHUMI:v7p5264/r26.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5264/r26.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v7p5264/r26.claim: Another says God guided each thing to what suits it.
JISHUMI:v7p5264/r26.anchor: وقيل: هدى كل شيء لما يصلح له

JISHUMI:v7p5268/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5268/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5268/r1.claim: The verse denies child and partner, contrary to Christians, dualists, and Magians.
JISHUMI:v7p5268/r1.anchor: وتدل على نفي الشريك والولد، خلاف قول النصارى، والثنوية، والمجوس.

JISHUMI:v7p5268/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5268/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5268/r2.claim: The Qurʾān is created because it is one of the created, measured things.
JISHUMI:v7p5268/r2.anchor: ويدل قوله: (وخلق كل شيء) أن القرآن مخلوق؛ لأنه من الأشياء المقدورة

MUQATIL:25:1-2/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:25:1-2/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:25:1-2/r5.claim: God alone possesses dominion over the heavens and earth.
MUQATIL:25:1-2/r5.anchor: الذي له ملك السماوات والأرض } وحده { ولم يتخذ ولدا

MUQATIL:25:1-2/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:25:1-2/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:25:1-2/r6.claim: This denies the claims of Jews and Christians that Ezra and the Messiah are God's sons.
MUQATIL:25:1-2/r6.anchor: ولم يتخذ ولدا } لقول اليهود والنصارى، عزير ابن الله، والمسيح ابن الله،

MUQATIL:25:1-2/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:25:1-2/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:25:1-2/r7.claim: God has no angelic partners in dominion; Arabs claimed angels were His partners and worshipped them, which God refutes.
MUQATIL:25:1-2/r7.anchor: ولم يكن له شريك في الملك } من الملائكة، وذلك أن العرب، قالوا: إن الله عز وجل شريكا من الملائكة،

MUQATIL:25:1-2/r8.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:25:1-2/r8.speaker: author
MUQATIL:25:1-2/r8.claim: God created each thing and determined it as it ought to be created.
MUQATIL:25:1-2/r8.anchor: وخلق كل شيء فقدره تقديرا } [آية: 2] كما ينبغى أن يخلقه.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p160#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p160#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p160#2/r1.claim: The opening relative is the predicate of an omitted subject, an appositive to the earlier relative, or an accusative of praise.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p160#2/r1.anchor: رفع على انه خبر مبتدأ محذوف أو على الابدال من الذى نزل

NASAFI-FULL:v3p160#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p160#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p160#2/r2.claim: God alone has dominion over the heavens and earth.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p160#2/r2.anchor: ﴿ له ملك السماوات والأرض ﴾ على الخلوص

NASAFI-FULL:v3p160#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p160#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p160#2/r3.claim: God has no child, contrary to the Jews' and Christians' claims about Ezra and the Messiah.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p160#2/r3.anchor: كما زعم اليهود والنصارى فى عزير والمسيح عليهما السلام

NASAFI-FULL:v3p160#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p160#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p160#2/r4.claim: God has no partner in dominion, contrary to the dualists' claim.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p160#2/r4.anchor: ﴿ ولم يكن له شريك في الملك ﴾ كما زعمت الثنوية

NASAFI-FULL:v3p160#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p160#2/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p160#2/r5.claim: God alone brought every thing into being, rather than the Magians' and dualists' attribution of creation to light and darkness, Yazdan and Ahriman.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p160#2/r5.anchor: أحدث كل شئ وحده لا كما يقوله المجوس والثنوية من النور والظلمة ويزدان واهر من

NASAFI-FULL:v3p160#2/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p160#2/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p160#2/r6.claim: An agent with all his attributes cannot be an object acted upon; this supports saying God is a thing and the Quran is created.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p160#2/r6.anchor: لمن يقول ان الله شئ ويقول بخلق القرآن لأن الفاعل بجميع صفاته لا يكون مفعولا له

NASAFI-FULL:v3p160#2/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p160#2/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p160#2/r7.claim: The verse is Nasafi's clearest proof against the Muʿtazila on the creation of human acts.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p160#2/r7.anchor: وهذا أوضح دليل لنا على المعتزلة فى خلق افعال العباد

NASAFI-FULL:v3p160#2/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p160#2/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p160#2/r8.claim: Here thing is restricted to what can be created, as the nearby verb indicates.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p160#2/r8.anchor: لفظ شئ اختص بما يصح ان يخلق بقرينة وخلق

NASAFI-FULL:v3p160#2/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p160#2/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p160#2/r9.claim: God prepared each thing for its proper use without defect; the human form is fitted to religious and worldly duties and interests.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p160#2/r9.anchor: فهيأه لما يصلح له بلا خلل فيه كما أنه الانسان على هذا الشكل الذى تراه فقدره للتكاليف والمصالح المنوطة به

NASAFI-FULL:v3p160#2/r10.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p160#2/r10.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p160#2/r10.claim: Alternatively, God decreed that each thing would remain until a known term.

QURTUBI-FULL:25:1-2/r21.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:25:1-2/r21.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:25:1-2/r21.claim: The statement of God's sole ownership magnifies Him.
QURTUBI-FULL:25:1-2/r21.anchor: قوله تعالى: { الذي له ملك السماوات والأرض } عظم تعالى نفسه.

QURTUBI-FULL:25:1-2/r22.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:25:1-2/r22.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:25:1-2/r22.claim: The denial of a son refutes claims that angels are God's daughters, ʿUzayr is His son, or the Messiah is His son.
QURTUBI-FULL:25:1-2/r22.anchor: نزه سبحانه وتعالى نفسه عما قاله المشركون من أن الملائكة أولاد الله يعني بنات الله سبحانه وتعالى. وعما قالت اليهود: عزير ابن الله جل الله تعالى. وعما قالت النصارى: المسيح ابن الله تعالى الله عن ذلك.

QURTUBI-FULL:25:1-2/r23.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:25:1-2/r23.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:25:1-2/r23.claim: God's sole sovereignty counters the worship of idols.
QURTUBI-FULL:25:1-2/r23.anchor: { ولم يكن له شريك في الملك } كما قال عبدة الأوثان.

QURTUBI-FULL:25:1-2/r24.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:25:1-2/r24.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:25:1-2/r24.claim: God's creation of everything refutes Magians and dualists who assign creation to Satan or darkness, and those who give creatures power to originate things.
QURTUBI-FULL:25:1-2/r24.anchor: لا كما قال المجوس والثنوية: إن الشيطان أو الظلمة يخلق بعض الأشياء. ولا كما يقول من قال: للمخلوق قدرة الإيجاد.

QURTUBI-FULL:25:1-2/r25.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:25:1-2/r25.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:25:1-2/r25.claim: God measured each created thing wisely as He willed, without heedlessness; His decrees extend through and beyond the Resurrection, so worship Him.
QURTUBI-FULL:25:1-2/r25.anchor: أي قدر كل شيء مما خلق بحكمته على ما أراد، لا عن سهوة وغفلة، بل جرت المقادير على ما خلق الله إلى يوم القيامة وبعد القيامة، فهو الخالق المقدر فإياه فاعبدوه.

QASHANI:25:2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:25:2/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:25:2/r1.claim: God subdues the heavens and earth beneath His dominion.
QASHANI:25:2/r1.anchor: يقهرهما تحت ملكوته، أوجد كل شيء موسوما

QASHANI:25:2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:25:2/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:25:2/r2.claim: Everything He brings into being bears the mark of contingency and testifies to its nonexistence in itself.
QASHANI:25:2/r2.anchor: أوجد كل شيء موسوما، يتعين بسمة الإمكان، ويشهد عليه بالعدم

QASHANI:25:2/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:25:2/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:25:2/r3.claim: He apportions each thing according to its capacity to receive some attributes and manifest some perfections, preparing each aptitude for the perfections He wills.
QASHANI:25:2/r3.anchor: على قدر قبول بعض صفاته ومظهرية بعض كمالاته دون بعض، أي: هيأ استعداداتهم لما شاء

RAZI-FULL:v24p41/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p41/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p41/r1.claim: God’s ownership of the heavens and earth points to His existence: His effects depend on Him, so this attribute properly precedes the others.
RAZI-FULL:v24p41/r1.anchor: لا طريق إلى إثباته إلا بواسطة احتياج أفعاله إليه

RAZI-FULL:v24p41/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p41/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p41/r2.claim: Everything in the heavens and earth depends on God for origination, persistence, essence, and existence, and He disposes of it as He wills.
RAZI-FULL:v24p41/r2.anchor: إشارة إلى احتياج هذه المخلوقات إليه سبحانه بزمان حدوثها وزمان بقائها في ماهيتها وفي وجودها

RAZI-FULL:v24p41/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p41/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p41/r3.claim: God takes no child: He alone is eternally worshipped, and no one inherits sovereignty from Him; this reinforces the opening and refutes Christians.
RAZI-FULL:v24p41/r3.anchor: فبين سبحانه أنه هو المعبود أبدا

RAZI-FULL:v24p41/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p41/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p41/r4.claim: God alone is divine; recognizing this cuts off fear and hope directed to other beings and refutes dualists and worshippers of stars or idols.
RAZI-FULL:v24p41/r4.anchor: والمراد أنه هو المنفرد بالإلهية ، وإذا عرف العبد ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v24p41/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p41/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p41/r5.claim: Al-Rāzī says “He created everything” includes human acts, since acts are things.
RAZI-FULL:v24p41/r5.anchor: يتناول جميع الأشياء فيتناول أفعال العباد

RAZI-FULL:v24p41/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p41/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p41/r6.claim: The verse also answers those who deny other gods yet claim to create their own acts, following the denial of partners.
RAZI-FULL:v24p41/r6.anchor: لما نفى الشريك كأن قائلا قال : ههنا أقوام يعترفون

RAZI-FULL:v24p41/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p41/r7.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v24p41/r7.claim: Al-Qāḍī objects that the verse cannot imply God creates human acts because scripture calls the servant a creator and calls God the best of creators.
RAZI-FULL:v24p41/r7.anchor: قال القاضي الآية لا تدل عليه لوجوه : أحدها

RAZI-FULL:v24p41/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p41/r8.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v24p41/r8.claim: Al-Qāḍī argues that because God praises Himself for creation, the verse cannot refer to creating evil.
RAZI-FULL:v24p41/r8.anchor: وثانيها : أنه سبحانه تمدح بذلك فلا يجوز أن يريد به خلق الفساد

RAZI-FULL:v24p41/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p41/r9.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v24p41/r9.claim: Al-Qāḍī argues that God’s praise for precise apportionment can refer only to good and wise things, not evil.
RAZI-FULL:v24p41/r9.anchor: وثالثها : أنه سبحانه تمدح بأنه قدره تقديرا ولا يجوز أن يريد به

RAZI-FULL:v24p41/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p41/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p41/r10.claim: Al-Rāzī relays al-Qāḍī’s argument that creation means apportionment, which appears only in bodies, not accidents.
RAZI-FULL:v24p41/r10.anchor: لأن الخلق عبارة عن التقدير فهو لا يتناول إلا ما يظهر فيه التقدير

RAZI-FULL:v24p41#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p41#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p41#2/r1.claim: Al-Rāzī answers that the servant-creator verses are countered by 39:62, “God is creator of everything,” and 35:3, “Is there any creator besides God?”
RAZI-FULL:v24p41#2/r1.anchor: فهما معارضان بقوله : { الله خالق كل شىء }

RAZI-FULL:v24p41#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p41#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p41#2/r2.claim: God may be praised for creating evil insofar as it displays the scope of His power to bring things from nonexistence into existence and extinguish them.
RAZI-FULL:v24p41#2/r2.anchor: لم لا يجوز أن يقع التمدح به نظرا إلى تقادير القدرة وإلى أن صفة الإيجاد من العدم

RAZI-FULL:v24p41#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p41#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p41#2/r3.claim: If creation applied only to bodies, the statement “He created everything” would wrongly ascribe creation to things that cannot rationally be said to be created.
RAZI-FULL:v24p41#2/r3.anchor: لو كان كذلك لكان قوله { خلق كل * شىء } خطأ

RAZI-FULL:v24p41#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p41#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p41#2/r4.claim: Creation is not repeated estimation: God originates each thing with measure and order, preparing it for what suits it and its proper purpose.
RAZI-FULL:v24p41#2/r4.anchor: إحداثا يراعي فيه التقدير والتسوية ، فقدره تقديرا

RAZI-FULL:v24p41#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p41#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p41#2/r5.claim: Humans are formed in balanced shape for religious and worldly duties and interests; every animal and inanimate thing is made in wise proportion for a fitting purpose.
RAZI-FULL:v24p41#2/r5.anchor: مثاله أنه خلق الإنسان على هذا الشكل المقدر ( المستوي ) الذي تراه

RAZI-FULL:v24p41#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p41#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p41#2/r6.claim: Divine estimation is knowledge and truthful disclosure, unlike human conjecture; what God knows will not occur cannot occur, or His knowledge would become ignorance and His truthful report a lie. Thus command and will do not always coincide.
RAZI-FULL:v24p41#2/r6.anchor: أما في حقه سبحانه فلا معنى له إلا العلم به والإخبار عنه

RAZI-FULL:v24p41#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p41#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p41#2/r7.claim: If an act is necessary once power and motive are complete, the servant’s act would necessitate God’s act; if not, it is either an uncaused possibility or requires a chain of determinants ending at the Necessary Existent.
RAZI-FULL:v24p41#2/r7.anchor: عند حصول القدرة والداعية الخالصة إن وجب الفعل

RAZI-FULL:v24p41#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p41#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p41#2/r8.claim: People seek knowledge and truth but often acquire ignorance and falsehood; explaining each error by an earlier error regresses, while self-caused ignorance is impossible, so all occurs by God’s pervasive decree.
RAZI-FULL:v24p41#2/r8.anchor: لكن الإنسان لا يريد إلا العلم والحق فلا يحصل له إلا الجهل والباطل

STUDYQURAN:25:2/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:25:2/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:25:2/r1.claim: For God's sovereignty, the commentary points to Sūrah 67, 67:1, and 36:83.
STUDYQURAN:25:2/r1.anchor: For God’s sovereignty, see Sūrah 67, “Sovereignty”; see also 67:1c; 36:83c.

STUDYQURAN:25:2/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:25:2/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:25:2/r2.claim: The rejection of God's having a child addresses Arab pagan claims of divine daughters and the Christian doctrine of Jesus as God's son.
STUDYQURAN:25:2/r2.anchor: the notion of God having a child, which includes both Arab pagan beliefs

STUDYQURAN:25:2/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:25:2/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:25:2/r3.claim: Measured it out translates qaddara followed by its cognate verbal noun taqdīr.
STUDYQURAN:25:2/r3.anchor: and the verb’s corresponding verbal noun

STUDYQURAN:25:2/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:25:2/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:25:2/r4.claim: Taqdīr includes both knowing a thing's measure and bestowing a measure, with senses of estimation and ordainment.
STUDYQURAN:25:2/r4.anchor: encompasses both knowing the measure of a thing and bestowing a measure upon a thing

STUDYQURAN:25:2/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:25:2/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:25:2/r5.claim: The term bears on created order, God's knowledge and power, and thus divine omniscience and omnipotence.
STUDYQURAN:25:2/r5.anchor: implications for the theological questions surrounding the order found in creation as well as both God’s Knowledge of things and His Power over them

STUDYQURAN:25:2/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:25:2/r6.speaker: al-Rāzī
STUDYQURAN:25:2/r6.claim: Al-Rāzī distinguishes human taqdīr as estimation from God's eternal, unchanging knowledge of each creature's whole existence from beginning to end.
STUDYQURAN:25:2/r6.anchor: Al-Rāzī notes that, as it concerns human beings, taqdīr is an act of estimation or assessment

STUDYQURAN:25:2/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:25:2/r7.speaker: IK and Q
STUDYQURAN:25:2/r7.claim: Other commentators stress taqdīr as ordainment or predestination of all that a creature was, is, or will be; it resembles qadar, one's allotted measure and the doctrine of predestination.
STUDYQURAN:25:2/r7.anchor: Other commentators emphasize the sense of taqdīr as ordainment

QUSHAYRI:v2p377#2/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p377#2/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p377#2/r6.claim: God alone owns the kingdom: He has no partner in His essence or created works and no likeness in His reality or attributes.
QUSHAYRI:v2p377#2/r6.anchor: تفرد بالملك فلا شريك يساهمه ، وتوجد بالجلال فلا نظير يقاسمه ؛ فهو الواحد بلا قسيم في ذاته

TAB-FULL:v17p395/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p395/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p395/r1.claim: The second الذي is an adjective of the first; both are nominative, with the first governed by تبارك.
TAB-FULL:v17p395/r1.anchor: الذي له سلطان السماوات والأرض ينفذ في جميعها أمره وقضاءه، ويمضي في كلها أحكامه.

TAB-FULL:v17p395/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p395/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p395/r2.claim: God's sovereignty means His authority and commands, judgments, and rulings prevail throughout the heavens and earth.
TAB-FULL:v17p395/r2.anchor: الذي له سلطان السماوات والأرض ينفذ في جميعها أمره وقضاءه، ويمضي في كلها أحكامه.

TAB-FULL:v17p395/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p395/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p395/r3.claim: Those under God's dominion must obey Him and not disobey Him.
TAB-FULL:v17p395/r3.anchor: فحق على من كان كذلك أن يطيعه أهل مملكته ومن في سلطانه، ولا يعصوه.

TAB-FULL:v17p395/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p395/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p395/r4.claim: This denies the claim that God took a child, including the pagan claim that angels are God's daughters; attributing a child to Him is a lie.
TAB-FULL:v17p395/r4.anchor: {ولم يتخذ ولدا} [الفرقان: 2] يقول تكذيبا لمن أضاف إليه الولد وقال: الملائكة بنات الله: ما اتخذ الذي نزل الفرقان على عبده ولدا

TAB-FULL:v17p395/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p395/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p395/r5.claim: This refutes pagan partners in divinity; their talbiya admitted a partner owned by God, but God has no partner in sovereignty to be worshipped alongside Him.
TAB-FULL:v17p395/r5.anchor: ويقول في تلبيته: " لبيك لا شريك لك، إلا شريكا هو لك، تملكه وما ملك: " كذب قائلو هذا القول، ما كان لله شريك

TAB-FULL:v17p395/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p395/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p395/r6.claim: People must dedicate divinity and worship to God alone, since every other object of worship is His creation and possession.
TAB-FULL:v17p395/r6.anchor: فأفردوا أيها الناس لربكم الذي نزل الفرقان على عبده محمد نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم الألوهة، وأخلصوا له العبادة،

SULAMI:v2p58#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p58#2/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p58#2/r1.claim: Whoever obeys God and prefers Him has a share in the kingdom of the heavens and earth.
SULAMI:v2p58#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطاء رحمه الله : له ملك السموات فمن أطاعه وآثره ملكه

SULAMI:v2p58#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p58#2/r2.speaker: النصرآباذي
SULAMI:v2p58#2/r2.claim: The one occupied with divine sovereignty becomes sovereign; the one occupied with kingship gains kingship and the kingdom.
SULAMI:v2p58#2/r2.anchor: وقال النصرآباذي : له الملك فمن اشتغل بالملك فإنه الملك

SULAMI:v2p58#2/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p58#2/r3.speaker: الحسين
SULAMI:v2p58#2/r3.claim: Al-Husayn describes successive orders of creation: one begins with light and proceeds through soul, spirit, form, names, qualities, time, measures, and more; another begins with time, power, substance, sound, and spirit. The hidden knowledge and precise measure belong to God alone.
SULAMI:v2p58#2/r3.anchor: قال الحسين : أول ما خلق الله تعالى ذكر ستة أشياء في ستة وجوه قدر بذلك

TABATABAI:25:1-2/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:25:1-2/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:25:1-2/r11.claim: Al-mulk/al-milk describes something’s dependence on another that may dispose of it as it wills, whether by ownership of its substance or by sovereign command and rule.
TABATABAI:25:1-2/r11.anchor: الملك بكسر الميم وفتحها قيام شيء بشيء بحيث يتصرف فيه كيف شاء

TABATABAI:25:2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:25:2/r1.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:25:2/r1.claim: Al-Rāghib distinguishes mulk, rule by command and prohibition over a people, from milk, control of what is possessed; the latter is broader, and every mulk is milk but not vice versa.
TABATABAI:25:2/r1.anchor: كما قال الراغب الملك - بفتح الميم وكسر اللام - هو المتصرف بالأمر والنهي في الجمهور

TABATABAI:25:2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:25:2/r2.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:25:2/r2.claim: Al-Rāghib says mulk is control of an object subject to judgment, while milk is the wider genus; some reserve milk for ownership of the substance and mulk for other rule.
TABATABAI:25:2/r2.anchor: فالملك بالضم - ضبط الشيء المتصرف فيه بالحكم

TABATABAI:25:2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:25:2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:25:2/r3.claim: The lām of exclusive possession means the heavens and earth are not self-sufficient in any respect; God alone rules and administers them absolutely.
TABATABAI:25:2/r3.anchor: واللام للاختصاص - يفيد أن السماوات والأرض مملوكة له غير مستقلة بنفسها

TABATABAI:25:2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:25:2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:25:2/r4.claim: An owner may take a child to help manage limited affairs or to inherit after death; God has power over everything and eternal dominion, so He needs no child, refuting pagans and Christians.
TABATABAI:25:2/r4.anchor: فإن الملك على الإطلاق لا يدع حاجة إلى اتخاذ الولد إذ اتخاذ الولد لأحد أمرين

TABATABAI:25:2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:25:2/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:25:2/r5.claim: A partner is needed only when one’s rule does not cover everything; God’s dominion encompasses every thing and aspect, refuting polytheists.
TABATABAI:25:2/r5.anchor: وكذا قوله تعالى بعده { ولم يكن له شريك في الملك } فإن الحاجة إلى الشريك

TABATABAI:25:2/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:25:2/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:25:2/r6.claim: Creation and determination show that all affairs return to God alone: things arise through prior and concurrent causes, which determine their existence and effects within the observed order.
TABATABAI:25:2/r6.anchor: أن الخلقة لما كانت بتوسيط الأسباب المتقدمة على الشيء والمقارنة له استلزم ذلك ارتباط وجودات الأشياء بعضها ببعض

TABATABAI:25:2/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:25:2/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:25:2/r7.claim: Since God alone creates, He alone determines and governs; absolute ownership entails creation, creation entails determination, and determination entails administration, establishing His sole lordship.
TABATABAI:25:2/r7.anchor: وقيام الخلقة به يستلزم قيام التقدير به، لكون التقدير متفرعا على الخلقة

TABATABAI:25:2-3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:25:2-3/r1.speaker: الوثنيون
TABATABAI:25:2-3/r1.claim: Although they acknowledged God’s universal ownership, polytheists held that He delegated partial sovereignty and lordship to their gods, making each a lesser lord beneath the Lord of lords.
TABATABAI:25:2-3/r1.anchor: كان الوثنيون مع تسليمهم عموم ملكه يرون أن ملكه للجميع وربوبيته للكل لا ينافي ملك آلهتهم وربوبيتهم للبعض بتفويضه تعالى ذلك إليهم

TABATABAI:25:2-3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:25:2-3/r2.speaker: المشركون
TABATABAI:25:2-3/r2.claim: The polytheists’ pilgrimage formula allowed an exception: a partner belonged to God, who owned that partner and what it owned.
TABATABAI:25:2-3/r2.anchor: فقد كانوا يقولون في تلبية الحج لبيك لا شريك لك إلا شريكا هو لك تملكه وما ملك

TABATABAI:25:2-3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:25:2-3/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:25:2-3/r3.claim: Universal ownership alone does not disprove their delegated gods, because they could imagine God retaining ownership while assigning some affairs to created partners.
TABATABAI:25:2-3/r3.anchor: فلذلك لم يكف قوله { الذي له ملك السماوات والأرض } لإثبات اختصاص الربوبية به تعالى قبالهم

TABATABAI:25:2-3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:25:2-3/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:25:2-3/r4.claim: Creation and determination necessarily entail governance, so God manages every thing and has delegated no affairs to another.
TABATABAI:25:2-3/r4.anchor: فاجيب عنه بأن الخلق له سبحانه والتقدير يلازمه وإذا اجتمعا لزمهما التدبير فله سبحانه تدبير كل شيء

TABATABAI:25:2-3/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:25:2-3/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:25:2-3/r5.claim: The verse first establishes absolute ownership to deny a child or partner, then explains that ownership through universal creation and determination, which entails God’s direct rule.
TABATABAI:25:2-3/r5.anchor: فقد تحصل أن قوله { الذي له ملك السماوات والأرض ولم يتخذ ولدا ولم يكن له شريك في الملك } مسوق لتوحيد الربوبية

TABATABAI:25:2-3/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:25:2-3/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:25:2-3/r6.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī omits other interpretations of this and the preceding verse because he sees no useful point in them.
TABATABAI:25:2-3/r6.anchor: وفي الآية والتي قبلها لهم أقوال أخر أغمضنا عن إيرادها لخلوها عن الجدوى

THALABI:v7p122#2/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p122#2/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p122#2/r10.claim: God owns heaven and earth, took neither child nor partner, created everything that can be called created, and measured, formed, and equipped each thing for its proper use without flaw or disparity.
THALABI:v7p122#2/r10.anchor: وخلق كل شيء مما يطلق له صفة المخلوق فقدره تقديرا فسواه وهيأه لما يصلح له، فلا خلل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p404/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p404/r1.speaker: ابن عباس، مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p404/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Muqātil say God took no son—neither ʿUzayr, Jesus, nor angels, as Jews, Christians, and polytheists claimed.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p404/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس ومقاتل: ثم عظم نفسه فقال: {الذي له ملك السماوات والأرض ولم يتخذ ولدا} عزيرا، ولا عيسى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p404/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p404/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p404/r2.claim: The denial of a partner in sovereignty answers the claim of idol worshippers.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p404/r2.anchor: {ولم يكن له شريك في الملك} كما قال عبدة الأوثان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p404/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p404/r3.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p404/r3.claim: Al-Kalbī says God has no partner to rival Him in greatness.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p404/r3.anchor: وقال الكلبي {ولم يكن له شريك في الملك} فيعازه في عظمته

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p404#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p404#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p404#2/r1.claim: كل means all that can be described as created.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p404#2/r1.anchor: {وخلق كل} أي مما يطلق له صفة المخلوق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p404#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p404#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p404#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the decrees governing creation run through the Resurrection and beyond it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p404#2/r2.anchor: {فقدره تقديرا} قال ابن عباس: فجرت المقادير على ما خلق الله تعالى إلى يوم القيامة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p404#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p404#2/r3.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p404#2/r3.claim: Al-Kalbī says God assigned every thing its form, endpoint, and lifespan.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p404#2/r3.anchor: وقال الكلبي: جعل لكل شيء خلقا، ومنتهى، وأجلا ينتهي إليه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p404#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p404#2/r4.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p404#2/r4.claim: Abū Isḥāq says God apportioned animals' needs and sustenance, determining everything wisely, including lifespan and livelihood.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p404#2/r4.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: خلق الله الحيوان وقدر له ما يصلحه ويقيمه، وقدر جميع ذلك لخلقه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p404#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p404#2/r5.speaker: آخرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p404#2/r5.claim: Others explain تقدير as proportioning every created thing and preparing it for what suits it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p404#2/r5.anchor: وقال الآخرون: سوى كل ما خلق وهيأه لما يصلح له

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:25:1-6/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:25:1-6/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:25:1-6/r5.claim: God created everything that can be described as created and assigned it its measure.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:25:1-6/r5.anchor: مما يطلق في صفة المخلوق { فقدره تقديرا } جعله على مقدار

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p468#2/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p468#2/r7.speaker: علي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p468#2/r7.claim: Ali says everything is measured by God's decree, down to the tiny gesture he illustrates by touching his fingertip to his tongue and thumbnail.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p468#2/r7.anchor: عن علي قال: كل شيء بقدر حتى هذه، ووضع طرف إصبعه السبابة على طرف لسانه، ثم وضعها على ظفر إبهامه اليسرى.

ELMALILI:25:1-3/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:25:1-3/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:25:1-3/r14.claim: In his rendering, God creates everything, assigns each its limit and measure, and prepares all its decreed circumstances.
ELMALILI:25:1-3/r14.anchor: Her şeyi yarattı da bir takdir ile her birinin hadd ü mikdârını tâyin ederek hepsinin mukadderâtını hazırladı

ELMALILI:25:1-3#3/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:25:1-3#3/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:25:1-3#3/r13.claim: God alone has total disposal over the heavens, earth, and everything above and below: creating, destroying, giving life and death, and ruling by command and prohibition according to wisdom.
ELMALILI:25:1-3#3/r13.anchor: bütün göklerin ve yerin mülkü hep O’nun gerek gökler ve gerek yer ve gerek bunlardaki yukarı ve aşağı bütün şeylerde mülk, yani tasarruf-ı küllî

ELMALILI:25:1-3#3/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:25:1-3#3/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:25:1-3#3/r14.claim: God has neither biological offspring nor an adopted child; this rejects the Christians’ claim.
ELMALILI:25:1-3#3/r14.anchor: Hem hiç veled edinmedi veledi olmaktan münezzeh olduğu gibi bir evladlık da edinmiş değil, Nasârânın dediği gibi değil

ELMALILI:25:1-3#3/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:25:1-3#3/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:25:1-3#3/r15.claim: God has no partner in sovereignty, contrary to the dualists; the ownership clause already implies this, but explicit restatement directly rejects those claiming two or three gods.
ELMALILI:25:1-3#3/r15.anchor: Hem mülkte hiçbir şerîki de yok Sineviyyenin dediği gibi de değil

ELMALILI:25:1-3#3/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:25:1-3#3/r16.speaker: author

ELMALILI:25:1-3#3/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:25:1-3#3/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:25:1-3#3/r19.claim: By an unfathomable measure, God assigned every thing its bounds and quantities and prepared all its decrees in accordance with His wisdom.
ELMALILI:25:1-3#3/r19.anchor: de künhüne erilmez bir takdir ile her birine bir hadd ü mikdar tâyin ederek hikmetine göre dilediği gibi hepsini bütün mukadderâtıyla hazırladı.

ELMALILI:25:1-3#3/r20.claim: Nothing is difficult for God: all things are created, owned, and subject to His power; each has a limit it cannot exceed, while His power has no limit, so no creature can become His partner.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:25:2/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:25:2/r1.claim: The verses answer Meccan polytheists’ claims about God and more broadly reject beliefs, ideas, and acts that undermine or deny divine oneness.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:25:2/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:25:2/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:25:2/r2.claim: Creation is not chaotic but follows a cosmic order: every living and nonliving thing performs its appointed function within God’s laws, which no power can violate.
